title: fix(lint): one-line fix lines for the slice-19 rule ids (two flow wrong-syntax ids, capability, liveness ledger, two page-field ids, list-view mode); os explain carries what they explained
body:
Part of #22161
Clause-②: no

Slice 19 of the card: the over-long `fix:` lines, continued in slices 11–17's shape, for the ids slice 16's report (`6140250582`) lists in `validate-capability-references.ts`, `lint-liveness-properties.ts`, `validate-page-field-bindings.ts` and `validate-list-view-mode.ts`, plus `lint-flow-patterns.ts`'s two wrong-syntax ids now that #19939 has finished. Each finding's `hint` (the CLI's `fix:` line, the runtime advisory's `hint`) of these 7 rule ids is now one remedy line of at most 200 characters, and what the lines used to explain is each id's `RULE_EXPLANATIONS` entry behind `os explain RULE_ID`. The card stays open: the last section lists what is left.

Claim: `6213957180` (the newest `Claim:` naming this branch; the only later-or-concurrent claim, `6213942673`, names slice 18's branch; verified before the first edit). No file of slice 18 (`data-model-rules.ts`) is touched.

## What changes

**One remedy line per finding.** Every hint the lint suite fires, before → after (count of distinct hints · length range). Measured with the push-preload census (an `Array.prototype.push` preload over the whole lint suite, plus an `Array.prototype.map` leg for findings built with `.map()`), at the base `6db53acd6` and at this branch:

| rule id | file | lint suite, before → after | runtime door |
|---|---|---|---|
| `flow-double-brace-interpolation` | `lint-flow-patterns.ts` | 18 · 297–1413 → 12 · 87–197 | `flow` write, 2xx advisory |
| `flow-bare-dollar-reference` | `lint-flow-patterns.ts` | 23 · 114–1234 → 11 · 83–198 | `flow` write, 2xx advisory |
| `liveness-ledger-unreadable` | `lint-liveness-properties.ts` | 1 · 270 → 1 · 82 (map leg) | only on an install that lost a ledger file |
| `capability-reference-unknown` | `validate-capability-references.ts` | 1 · 241 → 1 · 131 | CLI only |
| `page-section-count-not-multi-value` | `validate-page-field-bindings.ts` | 1 · 228 → 1 · 167 | does not fire on a `page` write |
| `list-view-filters-in-views-mode` | `validate-list-view-mode.ts` | 2 · 99–219 → 2 · 99–135 | CLI only |
| `page-field-unknown` | `validate-page-field-bindings.ts` | 24 · 129–206 → 23 · 47–94 | does not fire on a `page` write |

Measured and **not** changed: `liveness-planned-property` (slice 16 listed it at 230) is 3 · 1–88 today. No shipped ledger row carries an `authorHint`, so its line is the verdict's default. The file's over-200 id is `liveness-ledger-unreadable`, which the push census cannot see (its findings come from a `.map()`); the map leg measured it, so it is converted instead. Stated as a deviation from the claim's per-file count.

Counts that fall are lists and judge sentences that no longer make each hint distinct. The flow counts also include cases this slice added (a reference list too long for one line, in each slot kind).

**The flow ids keep the judge's spelling, and only where it evaluates.** Before this change, both flow hints spliced the spec value-slot or text-slot judge's whole remedy into the line: guards, the run user's null, callee and client sentences, literal-position and legacy-shape paragraphs, the list of text slots. After:
- **Value slot:** the line is the judge's own direct spelling, read out of the judge's remedy and never re-spelled here (`directSpellingAt`, matching the judge's two direct openings, ``Write `{x}` as ENVELOPE`` and the text-with-holes concatenation). FROM (681) `A value slot reads a CEL value envelope, … $source.id names $source, which is not one of the flow engine's own $ variables, … Write {source.id} as { dialect: 'cel', source: 'source.id' }. CEL refuses an absent variable or key … (the guarded form writes null).` TO (116) ``A value slot stores a bare `$` reference as written: write `{source.id}` as { dialect: 'cel', source: 'source.id' }.``
- **Where an envelope at the string's place would not evaluate** (a string inside an object or list literal, a legacy `assignments: [{ variable, value }]` shape, a `$User` path that never resolved), the judge's remedy opens differently. The line names **no** envelope and points at `os explain`, so it never prescribes an envelope that would be stored as data. For a double brace it deliberately does **not** point at the build's own value-slot refusal. That refusal reads the outer braces as literal text, so its spelling is `'{' + record.title + '}'`, not the hole the author meant; a test pins this as the control.
- **Text slot:** the `{{ }}` hole for each reference the engine binds. For any other `$` root, the remedy every refusal of one ends with: compute the value into a variable with an `assignment` node and write `{{ v }}`.
- **Literals and elsewhere:** the literal lines keep "neither `{var}` nor `{{ }}` resolves there. Write the value itself.". Where they are refused, and the list of text slots, moved to the entries.
- **Bound:** a list of references that would not fit in one line takes a fixed bounded line (`withinHintBudget`, `HINT_BUDGET = 200`).

**Lists are no longer echoed** (slices 11, 12, 14, 16 and 17's rule). `page-field-unknown` no longer appends `Object fields: …`; it names the nearest declared field with the package's one "Did you mean" helper (`suggestName`).

**`os explain` carries the rest.** Six ids gain an entry, so their `rule:` line now carries the pointer: `flow-double-brace-interpolation`, `flow-bare-dollar-reference`, `liveness-ledger-unreadable`, `page-field-unknown`, `page-section-count-not-multi-value` and `list-view-filters-in-views-mode`. `capability-reference-unknown`'s entry gains one sentence: a capability another installed package declares needs no change. The two flow entries share five paragraphs (the text slots, the literals, the CEL caveats, the filter operand, the no-envelope positions), written once. Every id already had a rule-id constant on the root barrel, so no published name is added and `Clause-②: no` holds.

**Nothing else moves.** Every `message`, rule id, severity and `path` is unchanged, and so is what each rule accepts or refuses. The rule-file hunks are `hint` expressions, comments, the new hint helpers and constants in `lint-flow-patterns.ts`, and the `suggestName` import.

### File surface: the claim's

The five rule files, their tests, `rule-explanations.ts` (entries for these ids only, inserted beside the capability entry and away from slice 18's data-model entries), and `.changeset/22161-s19-five-file-fix-lines.md`. **Pin sweep, repo-wide** (`git grep` of each id, its constant and every distinctive old phrase, docs and examples included): only `packages/lint/src` tests pin these hints, so no `packages/cli` or `packages/metadata-protocol` rider was needed. Every flipped flow pin keeps its structural half: each envelope the line prescribes, put back in the slot, still passes the value-slot judge, the build door, the flow contract and this rule with 0 refusals. What left the line is asserted absent there and present in the entry.

## The runtime wire

`lintFlowPatterns` is `CLI_AND_RUNTIME` with `runtimeTypes: ['flow']`. Measured at the door with `runRuntimeAuthoringRules` (a scratch probe of 12 writes, base rule sources vs branch), all 2xx `advisories[].hint`, FROM → TO:
- `flow-bare-dollar-reference`: a value-slot `$source.id` 681 → 116, `$User.Id` 681 → 121, `$User.Email` 742 → 198, a nested literal 1231 → 198, a legacy assignment 1030 → 198; a text-slot `$User.Id` 767 → 144, `$error.message` 114 → 83;
- `flow-double-brace-interpolation`: a value-slot `{{ }}` 746 → 116, a notify literal 297 → 137, a value no slot reads 362 → 158.

`validateCapabilityReferences` and `validateListViewMode` are `CLI_ONLY`. A `page` write runs 4 rules and neither page id fires there (0 findings, base and branch). `lintLivenessProperties` runs on `email_template`, `mapping` and `datasource` writes, but `liveness-ledger-unreadable` fires only when `@objectstack/spec` ships without a ledger file; not probed. No 422 changes.

## Verification (all at the merge head `bb6c6032d` unless noted; heavy runs via `os-verify-lock.sh`, verdict lines read)

- Lint suite: base `6db53acd6` 140 files / 6776 passed | 5 skipped; branch `b8c9c4ac1` 140 / 6788 passed | 5 skipped; merge head 140 / 6794 passed. VERDICT 0 each.
- Census: base 231 ids fire, 33 over 200 (32 on the push leg alone); branch and merge head 231 / 26, the difference exactly these 7.
- Lint build (`check-dts-emitted`) + `typecheck` (tsc + `check:test-typecheck` OK, 2 files / 6 errors / 2 pinned): VERDICT 0 at `b8c9c4ac1` and at the merge head.
- CLI unit tier (`--project unit`), branch `b8c9c4ac1`: 302 files / 4498 passed, VERDICT 0.
- `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` whole suite, branch `b8c9c4ac1`: 242 passed | 3 skipped files, 20598 passed | 19 skipped, VERDICT 0.
- `@objectstack/spec` repo project (`--project repo`, which reads `packages/lint/src` as a text corpus), branch `b8c9c4ac1`: 63 files / 1070 passed, VERDICT 0.
- `objectstack validate` (built CLI), branch `b8c9c4ac1`, on app-crm / app-todo / app-showcase / app-multi-package: exit 0 each, `rule:` lines 9 / 7 / 68 / 3; none of the 7 ids fires on the apps.
- Ablation (one shot from the committed `b8c9c4ac1`, `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` under the lock, a shell trap restoring `HEAD` by absolute path; the lint suite imports source, so there is no dist leg): `HINT_BUDGET = 200` → `2000` (anchor x1 → x0, replacement x0 → x1, blob `a2a5a375ea3f` → `8e143fdfd2cd`). Predicted before the run: exactly the two bound cases red. Observed: `lint-flow-patterns.test.ts` 2 failed | 227 passed, exactly those two. Restored blob == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty, status clean.
- Derived gates: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` (no paths), 62 families, run one by one with each exit code captured before any pipe; `--ran` reconciliation in the report.
- Control-character scan of every changed file and of this body: no match.

## Acceptance notes

- **The count question in the dispatch, measured.** The census on `main` (`6db53acd6`) says 33 ids over 200 = 3 repo-gate (`lint-startup-registry-verdict.ts`) + 24 in the files slice 2 fenced (PR #22448) + 6 author-time outside the fence. Slice 16's ledger counted only the last group (13 then, 6 after slice 17), so the two counts were each right about a different population.
- **The flow lines carry less than they did, on purpose and bounded.** At a position where no envelope at the string's place evaluates, the line now names no spelling. The `os explain` entry describes each such position, but cannot carry a per-string spelling. For a double brace there, the build's own refusal is no substitute (it keeps the braces as text, pinned above).

## Remaining for this card (census at the merge head, 26 over 200, by file)

- `data-model-rules.ts` (3 measured): `unique/legacy-organization-composite` 578, `unique/unscoped-declared-index` 380, `unique/double-declaration` 279. This is slice 18's file; slice 17 recorded 3 more of its ids as NOT MEASURED by the census.
- `lint-startup-registry-verdict.ts` (3, repo gate, not author-time): `startup-open-vocabulary-verdict` 972, `startup-verdict-assertive-wording` 972, `startup-source-unparseable` 254.

  - `validate-flow-template-paths.ts` (2): `flow-template-field-unprovisioned` 362, `flow-template-lookup-traversal` 316;
  - `validate-page-field-bindings.ts` (2): `page-field-unprovisioned` 362, `page-section-group-unknown` 279;
  - `validate-component-props.ts` (1): `component-props-invalid` 258;
  - `validate-filter-tokens.ts` (1): `filter-token-unknown` 259;
  - `validate-form-layout.ts` (1): `form-section-group-unknown` 275;
  - `validate-print-page-blocks.ts` (1): `print-page-block-unprintable` 362.
